name: Proletarian internationalism
summary: Proletarian internationalism holds that capitalism is a world system and that workers of all nations share one class interest, so revolutions are parts of a single global struggle that should end in worldwide stateless communism. It subordinates national loyalties and national struggles to that class struggle, opposes imperialist wars, and in the Leninist form demands support for oppressed nations' right to secede and for colonial liberation movements.
scope: The Marx-Engels to Lenin and Comintern line of internationalism: the Communist Manifesto, Lenin's Socialism and War (1915) and his 1920 theses on the national and colonial questions, as summarised in Wikipedia. It does not represent Stalinist socialism in one country, Trotskyist permanent revolution or Cuban internationalism, which are noted only where they split adherents. Statements on domestic policy not discussed in these sources are inferred from general Marxist principles and marked low.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The Manifesto and Lenin treat capitalist markets as the engine of exploitation and imperialist rivalry, to be replaced by social ownership and planning.

public-ownership.rationale: The Manifesto calls for centralising the instruments of production in the hands of the proletarian state.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: The Manifesto lists heavy progressive income tax and abolition of inheritance among the first measures of a workers' government.

unions-good.rationale: Workers' organisation is the basis of class unity, though Lenin warned unions must be led by revolutionary politics and not stay reformist.

property-fundamental.rationale: The Manifesto defines communism as the abolition of bourgeois property, so private property in the means of production is no inviolable right.

cut-welfare.rationale: Cutting social provision harms the working class that the doctrine exists to defend; welfare cuts are seen as bourgeois class policy.

worker-ownership.rationale: Social ownership of production by the working class is the aim of proletarian revolution in the Manifesto.

limit-guns.rationale: No settled view; adherents favour arming workers against the ruling class while opposing private gun culture, so split.

state-harmful.rationale: The state is held to be needed during the transition after revolution, so the claim that it is unnecessary and harmful is rejected, unlike anarchism.

empower-police-military.rationale: Lenin sought the defeat and overthrow of bourgeois governments, whose armies serve class and imperial ends; more funding is not supported.

decide-locally.rationale: Revolution is conceived internationally and centralised under a workers' state; Lenin saw federation as only a transitional form toward unity.

traditional-family.rationale: The Manifesto predicts the bourgeois family will vanish with capital and criticises it as resting on capital and private gain.

more-religion-public.rationale: Lenin warned against clerical and feudal forces in the colonial world; the tradition favours secular public life.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Internationalism opposes national and racial oppression and Lenin demanded special action against inequality between nations, though class is the priority.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: The Manifesto says national differences are fading and that workers have no country; national culture is not a goal in itself.

gradual-change.rationale: Lenin calls for converting the imperialist war into civil war and rejects reformist gradualism as opportunism.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Workers' unity across nations is central, and immigration restriction is seen as dividing the working class.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Lenin denounced the League of Nations as an instrument of the Entente powers; bourgeois international bodies are not trusted.

free-trade.rationale: Free trade is tied to capitalist expansion and imperialist division of the world, though Marx saw it as hastening capitalism's crisis.

nation-first.rationale: The Manifesto says workers have no country and the doctrine places the global class above any national interest.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-12): the old wording asked whether military intervention abroad is sometimes necessary to protect human rights, and this disagreement rested on opposing particular interventions or interventions by particular powers, which doesn't say it is never necessary.

reviewHistory.rationale: Lenin saw great-power wars as imperialist, with claims like defending Belgium treated as hypocrisy, so he would distrust rights-based intervention.
reviewHistory.author: claude-sonnet-5-5

reviewHistory.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-12): the old wording asked whether military intervention abroad is sometimes necessary to protect human rights, and this disagreement rested on opposing particular interventions or interventions by particular powers, which doesn't say it is never necessary.

open-borders.rationale: The goal is unity of workers across nations and a stateless world communism, though adherents differ on open borders under capitalism.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Marxists see technology as freeing production only under social ownership; problems are mainly social, so neither agree nor disagree.

revolution-justified.rationale: Lenin explicitly endorses civil wars of oppressed classes and revolution as the route to ending war and exploitation.

central-planning.rationale: Planning by the workers' state replacing market anarchy is the usual socialist-state aim, though internationalism texts are less detailed.

socialized-markets.rationale: Adherents split between those who see market socialism as a transitional tool and those who see it as capitalism.

tax-inheritance.rationale: The Manifesto lists abolition of inheritance among the measures after the workers take power.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Adherents back independence of dependent countries but see tariffs as a bourgeois tool; no firm stance.

state-directs-investment.rationale: The workers' state is to centralise instruments of production and direct them, per the Manifesto.

widespread-small-property.rationale: The Manifesto notes small property is being destroyed by industry and aims at social ownership, not distribution among small owners.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale is about abolishing wage labour, not money, and the statement now asks only about money; wage labour has its own statement.

reviewHistory.rationale: Wage labor is a form of exploitation to be ended in communism, though adherents see abolition as a distant stage.
reviewHistory.author: claude-sonnet-5-5

reviewHistory.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale is about abolishing wage labour, not money, and the statement now asks only about money; wage labour has its own statement.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: The Manifesto calls for centralising credit in the state through a national bank, the opposite of abolition and a free market in money.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Class collaboration is rejected as social-chauvinism and opportunism; workers' and employers' interests are opposed.

one-party-rule.rationale: Lenin sought a vanguard party leading working people, and the Soviet-aligned tradition held party leadership of the state, though positions varied.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Lenin treated tsarism as reactionary and feudal; hereditary rule is rejected.

democracy-best.rationale: Marx wanted to win the battle for democracy but adherents see bourgeois democracy as class rule; unclear on the literal claim.

workers-councils.rationale: Lenin held that the Soviet system best ensures equality of nations and called for working people's soviets, so councils are favoured.

right-to-secede.rationale: Lenin insisted that socialists of oppressor nations defend the right of oppressed nations to secede (s3). That right is claimed for nations, not for regions in general, so the agreement is moderate.

natural-rulers.rationale: The tradition rejects natural hierarchies of rule and holds that class domination is historical, not innate.

political-violence-never.rationale: Lenin sanctions civil war by oppressed classes and rejects pacifist positions.

war-builds-character.rationale: War between great powers is deemed imperialist slaughter for plunder, not an improving force.

separate-church-state.rationale: The tradition is secular and wary of clerical forces, with Lenin warning against clerical influence in liberation movements.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Lenin warned against Pan-Islamism and clerical forces; law grounded in scripture is rejected.

private-courts-defense.rationale: The state is a tool of class power, and privatising it would deepen capitalist control; the doctrine seeks a workers' state instead.

military-superiority.rationale: Lenin condemned great-power arms rivalry and defence of the fatherland in imperialist wars.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Internationalism opposes national exclusivism and requires equality of nations and peoples, uniting workers of all nationalities.

class-struggle-history.rationale: The Manifesto opens with class struggle as the engine of history, and internationalism rests on it.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Lenin said the real meaning of equality is the abolition of classes, which points to material equality beyond formal opportunity.

civilizational-union.rationale: Lenin warned against Pan-Islamism and religious or civilizational blocs; the tie is class, not shared civilization.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Collective class solidarity, not individual self-interest, is the ethic; bourgeois individualism is criticised.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Solidarity and class duty matter, but the doctrine does not rank duties over rights as a principle; unclear.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Marx saw capitalist industry as creating the conditions for socialism and developing productive forces, not as a disaster.

restore-past-order.rationale: The doctrine is forward-looking and aims to abolish the existing order rather than restore a lost one.

results-over-ideology.rationale: The tradition is explicitly ideological and treats pragmatism without class analysis as opportunism.

direct-action.rationale: Lenin urged using all legal avenues together with underground organisation, rejecting both pure parliamentarism and pure direct action.

means-match-ends.rationale: Lenin accepted civil war and discipline as means to a stateless society, not a prefigurative approach.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Marxism sees development of productive forces as necessary to communism and rejects primitivism.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Marx foresaw overcoming it under communism but Marxist-Leninist practice kept specialisation; adherents split on how and when.

production-for-use.rationale: Production for social need rather than private profit is the defining goal of socialism.

profit-exploitation.rationale: The Manifesto and the tradition hold that capital's profit comes from workers' unpaid labor.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Seizing political power as the ruling class and suppressing the old classes is central to the Marx-Lenin tradition of revolution.

collective-farming.rationale: Adherents favour collective forms as socialist goals but Lenin urged support for peasant movements, so details varied.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Lenin calls imperialism the highest stage of capitalism and sees the war as a struggle of great powers over colonies and markets.

taxation-theft.rationale: The Manifesto calls for heavy progressive taxation by the workers' state, so taxation is legitimate.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Collective class interests take priority, and the doctrine criticises abstract bourgeois equality of rights.

conscription.rationale: Adherents sought the defeat of imperialist governments but accepted armed defence of workers' states; no clear stand on conscription.

state-as-business.rationale: The state is conceived as a class instrument, and running it for profit with customers is opposed to socialist aims.

media-academia-power.rationale: Marxists locate power in capital and class rule rather than in universities and media, although they stress bourgeois control of ideas.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Internationalism asserts the unity and equality of all peoples; racial hierarchy is rejected.

organic-representation.rationale: Representation through trade bodies and families on corporatist lines is rejected in favour of class politics.

national-rebirth.rationale: National rebirth belongs to nationalist ideologies; the doctrine puts class above nation.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Lenin condemns great-power seizures of colonies and territory as imperialism.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Feudal personal loyalty is a pre-capitalist form of domination that the doctrine opposes.

bound-labor.rationale: Lenin urges support for peasants against landowners and feudal survivals.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: The tradition holds that ruling ideas serve the ruling class, though it also claims scientific status for Marxism.

universal-morality.rationale: Marxists see morality as class-conditioned, though internationalists claim universal human emancipation; contested.

single-common-good.rationale: Society is divided by classes with opposed interests, so a single common good in the existing order is an illusion.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Marxist internationalists generally opposed nationalism of this kind and historically fought for rights where people live, though Soviet policy varied.

revive-national-language.rationale: Language revival belongs to nationalism; internationalists back equality of languages but not as a state-building cause.

school-vouchers.rationale: Privatised education choice runs against social provision and collective ownership.

economic-freedom.rationale: Economic freedom as capitalist property rights is seen as the freedom of capital to exploit, not a condition for political freedom.

force-without-un.rationale: Imperialist force is condemned, but no stance on UN approval since the doctrine regards that body as bourgeois.

class-collaboration.rationale: Lenin attacks social-chauvinism and opportunism and calls for class struggle rather than partnership with the bourgeoisie.

dominated-front.rationale: Lenin supported bourgeois-democratic liberation movements in dependent countries while keeping communist independence and judged them part of the world struggle.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: The Manifesto criticises the bourgeois family and the tradition supports equality of women.

ban-interest.rationale: Not a Marxist-Leninist position; capital's exploitation is the problem, not interest itself, though adherents favour state credit.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Racial oppression is condemned and workers of all nationalities are to be united.

state-class-instrument.rationale: The Manifesto calls political power the organised power of one class for oppressing another.

elite-replacement.rationale: Conspiracy of replacement is a nationalist idea; internationalism treats migration as part of workers' class composition.

national-mission.rationale: Imperial or national missions to export a government are great-power imperialism, though the Bolsheviks sought world revolution.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Bourgeois political elites are seen as serving capital and social-chauvinists as betraying workers.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Eugenic state coercion is contrary to the doctrine's equal worth of all peoples.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Minimal state serving property is the bourgeois state the doctrine seeks to overthrow.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Racial separation contradicts the unity of workers of all nationalities.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Internationalism stresses equality of peoples and unity of workers regardless of nationality, though class framing differs from liberal rights.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Internationalism treats proletarian revolutions as parts of one global struggle and Trotskyists reject Stalin's one-country line, but the USSR itself held that socialism could be built in one country, so adherents split with a lean to agree.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Religious dietary law is outside the doctrine and clerical forces are criticised.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Stalin-era Soviet doctrine held the state must strengthen under encirclement, while other internationalists reject this; the strands are split.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Marxists see legitimacy in class terms and not in liberal consent; adherents are split.

trade-surplus.rationale: Mercantilist export aims belong to capitalist competition among great powers.

population-transfer.rationale: Lenin condemned oppression of nations and unity of workers across nationalities rules out forced removal.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Lenin explicitly endorses revolutionary civil war and force against the bourgeoisie, so this is rejected.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Class struggle, not competition between individuals and peoples, drives history, and national struggle is subordinated to the world class struggle.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Lenin advised underground organisation because the bourgeoisie violates legality, but doctrine does not address banning of parties; split.

separated-powers.rationale: Soviets and unified power of the working class are favoured over a bourgeois system of checks.

vanguard-party.rationale: Lenin says internationalist workers' parties must act as the vanguard of the proletariat and fight opportunist distortions.

priority-to-poor.rationale: The doctrine centres the working class and oppressed, though by class power more than moral priority.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Strike restriction attacks workers' organisation which is a basis of class unity.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Poverty is attributed to class exploitation and imperialism, not to population.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Internationalism unites workers of different nationalities and treats national divisions as bourgeois constructs.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Dictatorship over the former ruling classes is accepted but suspension in an emergency by a bourgeois government is condemned; split by whose government.

party-controls-media.rationale: Adherents split on party control of media under socialist states; the internationalist core does not address it.

party-commands-army.rationale: Communist traditions placed armed forces under party leadership, while internationalism texts opened do not address it; contested among strands.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Workers' unity across nations opposes barriers that divide workers by citizenship.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: The EU-style union is seen as a union of capitalist states; internationalism seeks workers' unity, not a bloc of capitalist states.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Executive command by a head of state is a bourgeois or monarchic form; the tradition rejects it.

clerical-rule.rationale: Lenin warns against clerical and feudal forces and Pan-Islamism; clerical rule is rejected.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Lenin explicitly says revolutionaries should want their own government's defeat in a reactionary imperialist war.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Adherents oppose imperialist military blocs but also support alliances among socialist states, e.g. Warsaw pact internationalism; split.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Adherents' stance varies with class interest; national unification is not itself a goal.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Secularism and a scientific worldview oppose teaching creationism.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Descent-based citizenship favours ethnic nationality; internationalism opposes it.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Lenin held that national liberation means little without revolutionary support and Soviet power; formal independence is not enough.

constituent-assembly.rationale: The Bolsheviks dissolved the assembly in 1918; adherents hold soviet power over parliament, but the matter is unclear.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Central bank independence is a bourgeois arrangement; the Manifesto calls for state control of credit.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Land claims as historic homeland belong to nationalism; internationalists support peace against imperialist war.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Marxists reject private property in the means of production altogether and not just subordinate it to a common good.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Internationalists are split between Trotskyist, left-communist and Leninist-Stalinist views of the USSR.

collective-defense.rationale: Adherents oppose imperialist alliances such as NATO but supported mutual defence among socialist states; split.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Lenin opposed clerical forces and Soviet practice curbed church power and property.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Lenin held that socialists of an oppressor nation must defend secession rights and that no nation is free if it oppresses others.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Divine descent of rulers is feudal and religious ideology rejected by the tradition. No cited source discusses this statement directly.

flat-income-tax.rationale: The Manifesto calls for a heavy progressive income tax.

character-from-environment.rationale: Marxist materialism holds that social circumstances shape consciousness and character.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The ruler above the law is a feudal or absolutist model rejected by the doctrine.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Rule by the few and the many in balance is a class compromise; the doctrine seeks rule of the working class.

leader-cult.rationale: Leader cult existed in Soviet practice but is condemned by Trotskyist and left strands; split.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Adherents split between Stalinist, Maoist and other views on whether class struggle persists under socialism.

land-redistribution.rationale: Lenin urges support for peasant movements against landowners and feudal survivals, including seizure of estates.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Claims on territory because co-nationals live there is nationalist expansion that internationalism opposes.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Punishing leaving a religion contradicts the secular, anti-clerical stance.

women-must-cover.rationale: Compulsory dress codes from religious law are rejected by a secular tradition that supports women's emancipation.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Lenin warned against Pan-Islamism and cross-border union based on kinship; ties are by class.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: The Bolsheviks opposed cultural autonomy as a program in favour of unity but supported national equality; split.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Historical materialism is a core Marxist premise, as stated in the tradition.

ban-cartels.rationale: Lenin sees monopoly as the nature of imperialism, to be overthrown by revolution rather than reformed by competition law.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Autarkic imperial blocs are an imperialist form; internationalism envisions a world economy transformed by revolution.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Lenin urged underground organisation but held revolutionary conditions must be present; the foco view is contested.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Lenin treats tsarism as reactionary and feudal, and the doctrine opposes feudal privilege.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Internationalism opposes nationalist narratives and puts the world proletariat at the centre of history.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Lenin condemned colonial rule and the enslavement of most of the world by a few powers.

patriotic-education.rationale: The Manifesto says workers have no country, and Lenin rejected defence of the fatherland; patriotic loyalty is nationalism.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Lenin holds that capitalism has reached monopoly imperialism and is heading toward war and revolution rather than lasting adjustment.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Lenin condemned great-power influence over former dependencies as imperialist exploitation.

delink-world-market.rationale: Lenin supported liberation movements but not autarky; adherents are split over delinking.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its own rationale does not support its value under the reworded statement: it cites only an upper stratum of workers, not most workers.

reviewHistory.rationale: Lenin traced social-chauvinism to opportunism among a privileged layer of workers in imperialist countries, as in Socialism and War.
reviewHistory.author: claude-sonnet-5-5

reviewHistory.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its own rationale does not support its value under the reworded statement: it cites only an upper stratum of workers, not most workers.
reviewHistory.author: claude-opus-5-5

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Racial and national oppression is condemned and equality of peoples demanded.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Marxists see formal rights as limited, but not necessarily opposed to them; split.

workers-nation.rationale: The Manifesto says the workers have no country and the doctrine organises the proletariat as an international class, not along national lines.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Lenin's 1920 theses demand the liberation of colonial and dependent peoples and denounce imperialist partition of nations, so treaties imposed on them carry no authority.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: The ideology is built on active class struggle and the conquest of political power by workers, so withdrawal is rejected.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Lenin's analysis of imperialism holds that finance capital keeps backward countries dependent and exploited by advanced ones.

native-born-offices.rationale: The Manifesto says workers have no country and the ideology subordinates national divisions to class unity.

party-own-road.rationale: Adherents split: Comintern practice demanded central direction while later strands defended national roads.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Lenin condemns annexationist wars and national chauvinism, so demanding territory back through war is rejected.

land-use-tenure.rationale: The Manifesto's first immediate measure is the abolition of property in land with rents applied to public purposes.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Lenin backs colonial liberation movements, and the USSR and Cuba justified arming movements abroad as internationalist duty, though the statement's 'hostile governments' framing is broader.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Adherents are split: the Brezhnev-era Soviet bloc cited internationalism to justify intervention, while Lenin's self-determination principle and Trotskyists oppose it.

democratic-peace.rationale: Lenin treats wars among bourgeois states, democracies included, as imperialist wars for colonies and markets.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: The Manifesto treats law as the will of the ruling class, so no general duty to obey follows; this is an inference.

non-intervention.rationale: The doctrine backs solidarity with revolutions and colonial liberation movements abroad, so absolute non-intervention is rejected.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Lenin demands unity of workers of all nationalities and denounces chauvinism, which excludes blaming a minority.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: The Manifesto attacks the bourgeois family and its property basis, though it does not call for ending legal marriage as such.

local-production.rationale: The Manifesto says national seclusion gives way to universal interdependence, so a mainly local economy is not the aim.

informal-organisation.rationale: Lenin's theses call for the vanguard party and permanent organisation, not small informal groups.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Workers have no country and class interests outweigh national ones, so national legal primacy is not a principle.

religious-nation.rationale: The doctrine rejects nationality as a basis of loyalty and Lenin opposes clerical forces.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Lenin's theses demand equality of nations and oppose great-power domination, so tribute to a leading power is rejected.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: The Manifesto says communism abolishes bourgeois property in the means of production, not the personal appropriation of the products of labour.

defeat-communism.rationale: The doctrine aims at worldwide communism and treats capitalism as the enemy; coexistence is at most tactical, never the goal of defeating communism.

religion-illusion.rationale: Marxist doctrine, which the Manifesto states in ch.2, treats religion as ideology that changes with material conditions and that communism abolishes.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: The Marxist-Leninist view is that capitalism developed the productive forces that make communism possible.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: The Manifesto links women's position to the bourgeois family and property relations and calls for their abolition.

socialized-care.rationale: The Manifesto calls for replacing home education and abolishing the bourgeois family; socialised domestic work follows in the Marxist-Leninist tradition.

cooperative-communities.rationale: The Manifesto criticises the utopian communities; Marxists want worldwide revolution and state-led transformation rather than isolated communes.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Communism is the sound basis for society in this doctrine; a third course is rejected as reformism or utopianism.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Lenin demands soviet power and suppression of counter-revolutionary and clerical forces, but the statement's order-preservation framing is not the doctrine's; adherents split.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Lenin's 1920 theses demand support for colonial liberation movements and condemn the oppression of dependent nations by imperialist states.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Lenin supports forcible overthrow of exploiting regimes, but on class grounds, not religious law; split.

participatory-democracy.rationale: The doctrine looks to workers' councils (soviets) as direct organs of popular decision making, though the vanguard party's role limits it.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Class is treated as the primary oppression and others as bound up with it; adherents split on whether they must be addressed together.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: The doctrine holds that class struggle is the central division and that left-right compromises between classes are false; the Manifesto rejects reconciling the classes.

alienated-labor.rationale: The Manifesto describes wage labour as exploitative and stripping work of its character, in the line of Marxian alienation theory.

social-market-economy.rationale: The Manifesto calls for abolishing bourgeois property rather than combining markets with social protection; reform of capitalism is the target of Lenin's criticism of social-chauvinists in s3.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Engels linked women's subordination to class society, but nature domination is not a theme in these sources and Marxists differ.

reification.rationale: Marx's analysis of commodity fetishism, central to the Marxist tradition, holds that capitalism presents social relations as relations between things; the listed internationalist sources do not use the term.

racial-franchise.rationale: The Manifesto and Lenin's theses make workers of all nations one class and oppose national and racial divisions among them.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Singling out a religious minority divides workers, which the internationalist sources oppose in favour of one class interest.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: The Manifesto aims to abolish bourgeois property so that capital no longer lives on the labour of others.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Marxists accept revolutionary and defensive violence; Lenin's Socialism and War supports just wars, such as defensive and revolutionary ones.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Socialism and War rejects national defence and nation as a basis of workers' politics; the Manifesto states workers have no country.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: The Manifesto grounds politics in material class struggle, not a spiritual contest of good and evil.

culture-before-state.rationale: Socialism and War subordinates national questions to class struggle, so national cultural renewal is not a prior task.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Lenin's theses demand equality of nations and oppose any national privilege, including one for a majority nation.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: The Manifesto has the proletariat rise to be the ruling class and win the battle of democracy; socialism without workers holding power is not socialism in this line.

municipal-property.rationale: The Manifesto calls for centralising the instruments of production in the hands of the state, not local community ownership.

person-over-state.rationale: The Manifesto holds that the free development of each is the condition for the free development of all, yet the class collective takes priority; adherents split.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Proletarian internationalism puts class above nation and race; workers of all nations share one interest, so organising by racial group is rejected.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Lenin in Socialism and War supports civil wars, wars of national liberation and defensive socialist wars, and opposes only imperialist wars, so a defence-only rule is rejected.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Internationalism puts class above nation, and Lenin's national theses define nations by oppression and self-determination rather than language alone; mild disagreement, low confidence.

communal-electorates.rationale: The doctrine calls for unity of workers across nationalities and religions, and the Lenin theses oppose clerical and communal division of the working class.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Lenin and the Bolsheviks published the secret treaties and demanded the abolition of secret diplomacy, which Socialism and War also attacks.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Lenin's Socialism and War urges workers to turn the imperialist war against their own governments and refuse to serve it, though he accepts wars of national liberation.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: The colonial theses demand support for oppressed nations and an end to imperialist exploitation, but the goal is abolishing capitalism rather than reforming its rules.

smash-state-machine.rationale: The Manifesto says communist ends are attainable only by forcible overthrow of existing conditions, and the Leninist line calls for dismantling the bourgeois state.

sacred-nation.rationale: The Manifesto states that workers have no country, and Lenin subordinates national loyalty to class interest, so a sacred nation is rejected.

religions-one-truth.rationale: The Manifesto says communism abolishes eternal truths and all religion, so a committed Marxist rejects the claim that religions express a shared truth.

workers-own-party.rationale: The Manifesto calls for organising the proletariat into a class and a political party of its own, distinct from bourgeois parties.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: The Manifesto's chapter on proletarians and communists treats religion and morality as products of class conditions, not eternal truths.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Lenin's national and colonial theses support autonomy and federation for oppressed nationalities as a step towards workers' unity.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: The labour theory of value is core to Marxist economics and the ideology's class analysis.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: The Manifesto says workers have no country, and Lenin opposed defence of the fatherland in imperialist wars.

decent-living-guarantee.rationale: Cutting social provision harms the working class that the doctrine exists to defend; welfare cuts are seen as bourgeois class policy. (Carried over from cut-welfare, "Welfare programs create dependency and should be cut.", with the value reversed, 2026-11-11.)

former-empire-equal-treatment.rationale: Lenin condemned great-power influence over former dependencies as imperialist exploitation. (Carried over from former-empire-influence, "A country should cultivate political and cultural influence in regions once ruled by its predecessor empire.", with the value reversed, 2026-11-11.)

missingStatements.text: Workers of all countries share a common class interest that outweighs their national loyalties.
missingStatements.rationale: The slogan "Workers of the world, unite!" and the Manifesto's claim that workers have no country state this as the core of the doctrine.

missingStatements.text: Socialists should support the right of oppressed nations to separate while urging their workers to stay united across nations.
missingStatements.rationale: Lenin states that socialists of oppressor nations must defend the right to secede while workers of all nationalities remain unified.

missingStatements.text: Socialists should refuse to support their own country in a war between great powers fought for colonies and markets, whichever side is attacked.
missingStatements.rationale: Lenin rejects defence of the fatherland in the imperialist war and calls social-chauvinism a betrayal of socialism.

missingStatements.text: A revolution in one country is part of a single worldwide revolution and should be backed by workers elsewhere.
missingStatements.rationale: The doctrine treats all proletarian revolutions as parts of one global class struggle, and the USSR and Cuba justified aid abroad as internationalist duty.

notes: Strands differ on socialism in one country (Stalin versus Trotsky), on self-determination (Lenin versus Luxemburg and later left communists) and on whether the USSR was a socialist state. Answers on domestic and modern issues are mostly inferred and low confidence.
